title: Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497): Node.js Brotli RCE Vulnerability Explained
content_md: Key Takeaways Node2Shell, CVE-2026-111497, is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, rated CVSS 9.2. The decoder ignores an invalid block-type switch, continues from a corrupted state, and writes past its buffer. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1 fix the flaw, while end-of-life lines 20.x and 25.x remain vulnerable. Bun up to 1.4.3 is affected, and distribution Node.js builds may need a patched system Brotli package. Attackers sending or serving crafted Brotli streams can crash services, leak memory, and execute code remotely. Successful exploitation lets attackers open reverse shells, steal cloud credentials, deploy cryptominers, and pivot to other systems. The Picus Threat Library includes the Node2Shell Web Attack Campaign to simulate CVE-2026-111497 attacks against your defenses. Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497, also tracked as HTTP2Shell) is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that Node.js bundles. It scores 9.2 (Critical) on CVSS v4.0 and has been shown to give remote code execution on an official Node.js build [1]. Node.js shipped fixes on October 21, 2026 and exploitation in the wild was confirmed on October 26. Article Link: Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497): No
